542919.one: Re‑rated from ~Rs 280 to ~Rs 306 as capacity‑expansion wins and strong earnings lifted the stock, while profit‑taking, regulatory notices and occasional earnings‑misses triggered sharp pull‑backs.
542919.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2025‑08‑07 – “Robust Q1 FY26 results with 28.2 % net‑profit growth” → price held steady around Rs 240 (steady‑to‑slight‑up).
  • 2026‑05‑11 – Q4 FY26 revenue up 16.4 % and PAT up 32.1 % → price jumped ≈ +20 % from Rs 234.7 (04‑Apr) to Rs 280.8 (11‑May).
  • 2026‑08‑04 – Share price hits 52‑week high; Q1 FY27 revenue +13 % → price rose to Rs 317.3 (08‑Aug).
  • 2026‑11‑05 – Q2 FY27 revenue +13.2 % and Gurugram EBITDA record 23.8 % → price sits at Rs 306.5 (02‑Nov).

De‑rating factors

  • 2024‑11‑04 → 2024‑12‑02 – No headline in the list; price surged +21 % (280 → 339.5) – cause isn’t clear from the headlines.
  • 2025‑01‑27 → 2025‑02‑24 – No matching news; price fell ‑26 % (315 → 233.5) – cause isn’t clear.
  • 2025‑03‑10 → 2025‑04‑07 – No matching news; price rose +23 % (229.5 → 281.3) – cause isn’t clear.
  • 2025‑12‑22 → 2026‑01‑19 – Around the same time as the 2026‑01‑23 “Should you be adding Artemis Medicare?” piece; price dropped ‑18 % (275.8 → 225.4).
  • 2026‑09‑21 → 2026‑10‑19 – Around the same time as the 2026‑09‑29 GST notice (₹11.11 Cr) and a 5.69 % drop on 30‑Sep; price fell ‑20 % (358 → 286.1).

Pivots & turning points

  • Feb 2026 – Signed 15‑year MSA to operate 650‑bed VIMHANS Hospital (South Delhi) – a major capacity‑expansion signal.
  • Mar 2026 – QIP announced to raise ₹700 cr to triple bed capacity.
  • Jul 2026 – 300‑bed Raipur management deal – further geographic expansion.
  • Aug 2026 – Capital raise via equity shares approved; new independent director appointed (Dr Gyani).
  • Sep 2026 – GST notice (₹11.11 cr) – first regulatory penalty, followed by a short‑term price dip.

What moves this stock

  • Capacity‑expansion announcements (new hospital contracts, QIP, bed‑addition plans) → strong upside.
  • Quarterly earnings beats (revenue & PAT growth, record EBITDA) → immediate price rallies.
  • Regulatory or financial notices (GST notice, capital‑raise news) → prompt sell‑offs.

544432.one: IGCL surged from its IPO debut at Rs 111 to a 2‑year high of Rs 115 in Aug 2025, then slid to Rs 61 by Nov 2026 as monsoon‑linked demand worries and mixed earnings eclipsed early‑stage growth catalysts.
544432.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Jul 2‑3 2025 – IPO listing: Shares opened flat at the top of the price band (Rs 111). The market priced the company at the high end of the band, signalling confidence in the IPO fundamentals.
  • Feb 26 2026 – MoU with ICAR‑IARI (PM Fellowship): Stock jumped ~6% the same day, reflecting investor enthusiasm for a government‑backed climate‑resilient agriculture partnership.
  • Jul 11 2026 – MD Sanjay Aggarwal wins Visionary Leader Award: Share price rallied ~26% over the next month (59.39 → 74.55), the strongest 4‑week gain, as the award highlighted strong leadership and future growth prospects.

De‑rating factors

  • Nov 3 – Dec 1 2025: Price fell ~20% (102.41 → 82.45). No headline coincides; the cause isn’t clear from the news feed.
  • Dec 22 2025 – Jan 19 2026: ~20% drop (82.05 → 65.45) around the time the board re‑appointed two independent directors (Dec 28) and a market‑watch article questioned fundamentals (Jan 12). The timing suggests investor scepticism despite the governance update.
  • Feb 23 – Mar 23 2026: ~17% slide (65.96 → 54.96) with no direct news link; the move remains unexplained.
  • May 4 – Jun 1 2026: ~18% decline (69.18 → 56.53) despite earlier partnership news; the driver is unclear.
  • Aug 31 – Sep 28 2026: ~25% plunge (72.89 → 54.62) coinciding with the pre‑announcement of Q2 FY27 outlook (Sep 10) and a subsequent 8.48% daily dip (Sep 15), indicating market anxiety ahead of the November earnings release.

Pivots & turning points

  • June 2025: SEBI approval and IPO launch (price band Rs 105‑111).
  • Aug 19 2025: Q1 revenue surge +43% (B2B growth) – first major earnings catalyst.
  • Feb 26 2026 & Apr 9 2026: Strategic MoU and partnership with ICAR‑IARI to develop climate‑resilient products.
  • Jul 2026: Leadership award boosting sentiment.
  • Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 results (24% profit rise, 205% revenue jump) – a decisive earnings turnaround after a weak monsoon‑driven FY27 Q1.

What moves this stock

  • Government‑linked collaborations (e.g., ICAR‑IARI MoU) trigger short‑term rallies.
  • Leadership recognitions (MD award) produce the strongest upside bursts.
  • Earnings surprises and monsoon‑driven demand outlooks drive sharp downside moves, especially when results miss market expectations.

540078.one: Re‑rated from a low of Rs 84.4 to a high of Rs 239.9 as a series of capacity‑expansion announcements and blockbuster Q1‑FY27 earnings lifted the stock, while a few unexplained dips left the downside unclear.
540078.html:
Re‑rating factors (price rises linked to news)

  • 28‑30 Jan 2026 – Boisar plant start‑up & capacity boost – price climbed from ≈ Rs 108 (Nov 2025) to Rs 112.1 (Nov 2025) and then to Rs 117.85 by Feb 2026.
  • 4‑5 Jun 2026 – ₹3.5 Cr investment adds 2,550 MT/yr at Khalapur – the stock began a steady ascent that fed into the July‑August rally.
  • 11‑12 Aug 2026 – 3,550 MT capacity addition announced – ≈ +27 % jump from Rs 145.95 (20 Jul) to Rs 185.5 (17 Aug).
  • 15‑19 Aug 2026 – Q1 FY27 results (net profit +566 %, EBITDA +210 %) – reinforced the August surge; the market rewarded the profit‑margin breakout.
  • 29 Apr 2026 – Entry into IBC manufacturing – modest uptick seen in the subsequent weeks, supporting the broader up‑trend.
  • 31 Oct 2026 – H1 EBITDA margin more than doubles; Q2 FY27 PAT Rs 6.10 Cr – price jumped ≈ +34 % from Rs 179.2 (14 Sep) to the 2‑year high Rs 239.9 (12 Oct).
  • 12 Oct 2026 – Share price up 8.11 % (upper‑circuit news) – immediate price spike on the same day.

De‑rating factors (price falls linked to news)

  • 9 Feb 2026 → 9 Mar 2026 – ‑19 % slide (Rs 115.14 → Rs 92.8) – no headline in the list coincides; cause isn’t clear from the available news.

Pivots & turning points

  • Capacity expansions: Boisar (Jan 2026), Khalapur (+2,550 MT, Jun 2026), new 3,550 MT addition (Aug 2026).
  • Product‑line diversification: entry into IBC sector (Apr 2026).
  • Earnings inflection: Q1 FY27 profit surge (Aug 2026) and H1 margin doubling (Oct 2026).
  • Corporate actions: ₹15.1 cr warrant issue EGM (Nov 2026) and secretarial auditor resignation (Oct 2026).

What moves this stock

  • Capacity‑expansion announcements – each new MT‑year addition has sparked double‑digit rallies.
  • Earnings beats with margin expansion – Q1‑FY27 profit (+566 %) and H1 EBITDA margin > 14 % have produced the strongest price jumps.
  • Strategic product‑line moves (e.g., IBC entry) and market‑wide events (upper‑circuit trading) provide secondary catalysts.

Overall, Mitsu Chem Plast’s price action over the past two years is driven primarily by tangible growth‑capacity news and exceptional earnings, while occasional unexplained dips remain outside the visible headline timeline.

543331.html:
One‑line story – From a 2‑year high of ₹101.9 in Nov 2024, Meghmani Organics slid to a low of ₹39.4 in Mar 2026, then recovered to ₹54.3 in Nov 2026 as earnings‑driven optimism alternated with margin‑pressure headlines.

Re‑rating factors (price rises)

Date News Price reaction
 2025‑05‑05 → 2025‑06‑02 “Fundamental Stock Pick: Target ₹145” (7 Feb 2025) and “Stock‑talk: good harvest” (29 Jun 2025) – upbeat analyst coverage. +28 % (₹70.85 → ₹91.07)
 2026‑07‑29 → 2026‑08‑10 Q1 FY27 net profit ₹482 M vs ₹127 M YoY (29 Jul 2026) plus “Share price rises 9.38 % today” (10 Aug 2026). +35 % (₹46.90 → ₹63.23)
 2026‑11‑04  Q2 FY27 PAT up 193 % to ₹33.88 Cr; revenue +18 % (multiple releases on 4 Nov 2026). Small uptick to current ₹54.27 (from ₹52.62 in Aug 2026).

De‑rating factors (price falls)

Date News Price reaction
 2024‑11‑25 → 2024‑12‑23 No headline in the list aligns; cause unclear. –20 % (₹97.05 → ₹77.74)
 2025‑01‑27 → 2025‑02‑24 No matching news; cause unclear. –19 % (₹77.14 → ₹62.18)
 2026‑02‑09 → 2026‑03‑09 “Takes on some risk with its use of debt” (7 Feb 2026) and Q3 FY26 revenue report (3 Feb 2026) flagging cost pressure. –20 % (₹54.24 → ₹43.34)
 2026‑05‑14  Q4 net profit falls 60 % to ₹80 M (margin pressure). Price slipped from ₹58.5 (May) to ₹52.62 (Aug).

Pivots & turning points

  • Nov 2025: Brazil subsidiary launched – first South‑American foothold.
  • Jan 2026: ₹3.63 Cr green‑power deal – diversification into renewable energy.
  • May 2025: Nano‑fertiliser clearance for subsidiary (5 May 2026) – new product line.
  • Jul 2026: Q1 profit surge (₹482 M) – demonstrates earnings upside.
  • Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 profit up 193 % – strong pigment recovery.

What moves this stock

  1. Earnings surprises / profit surges – Q1 FY27 (July 2026) and Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) triggered sharp rallies.
  2. Strategic expansions – Brazil entry (Nov 2025) and green‑power investment (Jan 2026) generate positive sentiment.
  3. Cost‑pressure or debt‑risk news – Feb 2026 debt‑risk story and Q4 profit drop (May 2026) lead to noticeable sell‑offs.

Overall, Meghmani Organics reacts most strongly to clear earnings beats and strategic growth announcements, while margin‑pressure or financing concerns pull the share sharply lower.

534425.one: Re‑rated from Rs 166.97 (Nov 2024) to Rs 137.58 (Nov 2026) as fresh brand launches, aggressive outlet roll‑outs and a leadership hand‑over lifted the stock, while earnings misses and circuit‑break news pulled it down.
534425.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 17 Dec 2024 – Launch of the new “Bizarre Asia” restaurant in Kolkata → stock rallied toward its 2024‑11 peak of Rs 166.97.
  • 20 Dec 2024 – 16th brand announced for international expansion → helped sustain the high‑price level.
  • 24 Sep 2025 – Speciality’s Durga Puja 2025 menu rollout → price jumped ~19 % in September (123.76 → 147.03).
  • 20 May 2026 – FY‑26 net‑profit rise & FY‑27 15 % revenue‑growth target → price surged ~20 % in June (107.9 → 130).
  • 08 Jul 2026 – Opening of “Gong” flagship in Bandra → price climbed ~19 % from early‑July to early‑August (122.38 → 145.17).
  • 10 Aug 2026 – Q1‑FY27 profit up 29.6 % (₹7 cr) and sales +18 % → reinforced the July‑August rally.
  • 13 Aug 2026 – Avik Chatterjee appointed CEO → market viewed the change as a fresh growth catalyst, supporting the upward trend.

De‑rating factors

  • 27 Jan – 24 Feb 2025 – 19 % fall (154.48 → 125.46); no headline aligns, cause unclear.
  • 03 Nov – 01 Dec 2025 – 14 % decline (136.88 → 118.16); no matching news, cause unclear.
  • 21 Oct 2026 – Lower‑circuit alert (price dip) – no specific event in headlines, cause unclear.
  • 13 Aug 2026 – “Share price fall in micro‑cap segment” headline – coincided with the CEO change, suggesting short‑term profit‑taking.

Pivots & turning points

  • Dec 2024: 16th brand launch for overseas growth.
  • Aug 2025: Planned outlets in Abu Dhabi & Dubai – first Gulf entry.
  • Aug 2025: CTO Sandiip Kothaari hired – tech‑focused upgrade.
  • May 2026: FY‑26 profit surge & FY‑27 growth roadmap.
  • Aug 2026: Avik Chatterjee takes over as CEO.
  • Oct 2026: ₹200‑cr expansion plan targeting 200 outlets by FY30.

What moves this stock

  • New brand or flagship restaurant launches (e.g., Bizarre Asia, Gong) – strong positive reaction.
  • Robust earnings/ profit beats (FY‑26 net‑profit rise, Q1‑FY27 profit jump) – market rewards with price gains.
  • Strategic leadership or expansion announcements (CEO change, Gulf entry, 200‑outlet plan) – act as catalysts for rallies; absent or negative news (circuit‑break alerts) tend to trigger sell‑offs.

539551.one: Re‑rated from ~Rs 1,270 (Nov 2024 low) to ~Rs 1,900 (Nov 2026) as earnings beats and aggressive expansion (land deal, UK acquisition) lifted the stock, while mixed Q1 results and debt‑fundraising worries pulled it back.
539551.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Feb 14 2025 – Q3 FY27 results: Net profit +3 % and revenue +14 % → price rose from ≈ Rs 1,397 (Feb 17) to ≈ Rs 1,664 (Mar 17) (+19 %).
  • Jun 4 2025 – Zee Business story: Income up 18 % and operating profit up 23 % → price jumped from ≈ Rs 1,744 (May 26) to a 4‑week high of Rs 2,263 (Jun 23) (+30 %).
  • Oct 31 2025 – UK acquisition of Practice Plus Group (≈ Rs 2,200 cr): Follow‑on Q2 FY26 profit +30 % (Nov 14) → price climbed from ≈ Rs 1,735 (Oct 20) to ≈ Rs 2,043 (Nov 17) (+18 %).

De‑rating factors

  • Jul 7 2025 – Mixed Q1 FY26 results (profit down 2 %) and debt‑fundraising review (Jul 28): price fell from ≈ Rs 2,007 to ≈ Rs 1,737 (Aug 4) (‑13 %).

Pivots & turning points

  • Apr 5 2025 – O&M pact with Kammavari Sangham (110‑bed hospital).
  • Apr 7 2025 – Launch of “Aarogyam” quick‑check program for youth.
  • Jun 24‑25 2025 – ₹246 cr land acquisition on Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru.
  • Oct 31 2025 – Entry into UK market via Practice Plus Group purchase (₹2,200 cr).
  • Dec 15 2025 – Announcement of de‑merger to sharpen focus on preventive care.
  • Jan 17 2026 – Incorporation of new subsidiary for North‑India expansion.
  • Nov 4‑5 2026 – NCLT approval for clinic de‑merger, preserving tax liabilities.

What moves this stock

  • Earnings beats & profit jumps (Q3 2025, Q2 2025/26) trigger strong upside.
  • Strategic expansion announcements (large land deals, UK acquisition, O&M contracts) generate fresh buying interest.
  • Mixed results or financing concerns (Q1 2025 dip, debt‑fundraising review) prompt short‑term pull‑backs.

543687.one: Re‑rated from Rs 362 in Nov‑24 to Rs 244 in Nov‑26 as a branding‑driven rally in early‑2026 was erased by monsoon‑linked earnings weakness and margin pressure later in the year.
543687.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 15‑21 Apr 2026 – Brand‑ambassador & capacity push – Rohit Sharma was named brand ambassador and the company announced capacity expansion. Share price rose from ~₹240 (Feb 2026) to ₹269.5 by May 2026 (+≈12%).
  • 24 Sep 2026 – FY26 record revenue – FY26 results showed a record ₹11,380 mn turnover. The stock climbed to ~₹295 by late‑Sep 2026 (+≈10%).

De‑rating factors

  • 27 Jan 2025 → 24 Feb 2025 – Unexplained plunge – Price fell 27 % (₹247.8 → ₹180.5). No headline aligns with this move.
  • 13 Oct 2025 → 10 Nov 2025 – Unexplained drop – Price slipped 20 % (₹300.6 → ₹242.1). No matching news.
  • 4 Nov 2026 → 7 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 earnings pain – Q2 FY27 showed a 24 % profit decline and 5.7 % revenue dip; the stock fell to ₹243.6 from the August high of ₹265.5 (≈‑8 %).

Pivots & turning points

  • Apr 2026: Strategic shift to premium branding & capacity build‑out (Rohit Sharma ambassadorship).
  • Sep 2026: Operational turnaround reflected in record FY26 revenue.
  • Nov 2026: Seasonal monsoon headwinds and margin compression in the technical segment hurt Q2 FY27 results.

What moves this stock

  • Brand‑building announcements (e.g., celebrity ambassador, capacity expansion) generate short‑term rallies.
  • Strong top‑line news (record revenue, robust H1 growth) lift the share modestly but are quickly offset if not accompanied by profit upside.
  • Weak earnings or profit declines, especially tied to monsoon‑related demand and margin pressure, trigger sharp sell‑offs.

Note: Several of the larger 4‑week moves (Dec 2024‑Jan 2025, Jan‑Feb 2025, May‑Jun 2025, Jul‑Aug 2025, Oct‑Nov 2025) have no corresponding headline in the provided list, so the cause isn’t clear from the available news.

544054.html:
One‑line story: De‑rated from a 2‑yr high of Rs 680.55 to Rs 188.46 as occasional commercial wins and land‑bank expansions were eclipsed by sharp profit falls and a swelling debt load.

Re‑rating factors (price rises)

  • 14 Nov 2025 – “One Business Bay” commercial launch – stock jumped ~6% on the same day.
  • 29‑30 Jan 2026 – Q3 FY26 operational record & strong commercial traction – shares rose around the same time (price moved up in early‑2026).
  • 16 Apr 2026 – Acquisition of a Dadar‑West plot (₹100 cr GDV) – shares jumped 15‑16% intraday; the 4‑week rally from 23 Mar → 20 Apr (+33%) lines up with this deal.
  • 21 Sep 2026 – Momentum‑stock rally after a series of land‑bank updates – stock surged ≈13% on the day, reflecting market appetite for expansion news.

De‑rating factors (price falls)

  • 13 Jan – 10 Feb 2025 – 4‑week slide ‑36% – no headline aligns; cause isn’t clear from the list.
  • 30 May 2026 – Q4 net profit down 41% – price fell ≈21% in the following 4‑week window (05 May → 01 Jun).
  • 31 Oct 2026 – Q2 FY27 results: PAT down 30%, debt up to ₹800 cr – the 4‑week decline ‑23% (21 Sep → 19 Oct) coincides with this earnings disappointment.
  • 01 Jun 2026 – Mahim land acquisition (₹75 cr) – stock slipped ~4% (minor drag on the same week).

Pivots & turning points

  • Land‑bank build‑out: Prabhadevi (Feb 2026), Dadar‑West (Apr 2026), Mahim (Jun 2026).
  • Commercial project launches: Suraj Aureva (Jul 2025), Suraj Park View 1 (Sep 2025), One Business Bay (Nov 2025).
  • Award: “India’s Best Residential Developer 2025” (12 Dec 2025) – short‑term sentiment boost.
  • Earnings volatility: Q3 FY26 beat (Jan 2026) vs. Q4 profit plunge (May 2026) and Q2 FY27 loss (Oct 2026).

What moves this stock

  • Land‑acquisition announcements (especially high‑GDV parcels) trigger immediate double‑digit upside.
  • Commercial project launches and awards give short‑term spikes (≈5‑6%).
  • Quarterly earnings surprises—especially profit declines or widening debt—prompt sharp downside moves.

539118.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 284.9 to Rs 339.0 as strong earnings, bonus issues and aggressive share‑buybacks repeatedly lifted the stock.*
539118.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 2025‑02‑06 – Q3 FY25 results beat expectations; share price hit the 20 % upper circuit (price ~ 264 → 284 later).
  • 2025‑05‑22 – “What sparked 13 % jump?” article; stock rose from 229 to 284 (+24 % in 4 weeks).
  • 2025‑07‑04 – 1:1 bonus issue approved; price climbed from 278 to 318 (+14 % in 4 weeks).
  • 2026‑02‑05 – Q3 FY26 profit up 9 % with dividend; price jumped from 244 to 291 (+19 % in 4 weeks).
  • 2026‑08‑04 – Q1 FY27 profit surged 61 % and board approved a ₹280 cr buy‑back at ₹320; price surged from 232 to 296 (+28 % in 4 weeks).
  • 2026‑11‑02/03 – Q2 FY27 PAT more than doubled, EBITDA margin to 23 %; buy‑back window opened; price rose from 280 to 339 (+21 % in 4 weeks).

De‑rating factors

  • 2026‑03‑02 → 2026‑03‑30 – Stock fell from 274 to 231 (‑16 %); no headline directly matches, so the cause isn’t clear from the provided news.
  • 2026‑05‑18 – Q4 profit slipped ≈ 3 % as costs rose; price slipped from 285 to 265 (‑7 % in the month).

Pivots & turning points

  • 2024‑12‑10 – Purchase of a 5 lakh sq ft trans‑hipment hub in Bengaluru (capacity boost).
  • 2025‑07‑13 – Initiative to recruit drivers in hinterland (addressing skilled‑driver shortage).
  • 2026‑05‑20 – Set 6‑7 % volume‑growth target with fleet expansion.
  • 2026‑05‑25 – Order of 715 vehicles from Ashok Leyland (fleet upgrade).
  • 2026‑08‑04 – ₹280 cr share‑buyback approved (capital return).
  • 2026‑10‑24 → 10‑27 – Buy‑back opened at ₹320 (further price support).

What moves this stock

  • Earnings surprises & margin expansion – strong Q‑results repeatedly trigger 15‑30 % jumps.
  • Corporate actions – bonus issues and especially large‑scale share buy‑backs lift the price sharply.
  • Capacity & fleet upgrades – hub acquisitions, vehicle orders and volume‑growth targets are rewarded, while cost‑pressured quarters can drag the stock down.

544543.one: Round‑trip from ~₹70 at IPO to a peak of ₹71.38 in Oct 2026 and back to ~₹65 now, driven by large infrastructure orders and post‑IPO pricing quirks, with several moves unexplained by headlines.
544543.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Oct 1 2025 – IPO debut at a 21 % discount – shares opened sharply lower, but the “discount‑buy‑the‑dip” narrative helped the price climb from ~₹60 to ~₹70 by early Nov (+16 % over 4 weeks).
  • Feb 7 2026 – Q3 FY26 results (strong revenue, deleveraging) – price rose from ~₹54 to ~₹62 by Feb 23 (+15 %).
  • Feb 26 2026 – Rs 36 cr BHEL fabricated‑steel order – reinforced the Feb rally, supporting the same +15 % move.
  • Sep 16 2026 – Rs 72.94 cr Tata Projects order – shares jumped 4.96 % on the day and fed into a 38 % surge from ₹51.9 to ₹71.38 by Oct 12.
  • Sep 25 2026 – Rs 25 cr Tata Projects order and Sep 29 2026 – Rs 249.83 mn steel orders – added momentum to the same Oct‑month rally.
  • Oct 12 2026 – price‑band “hitters” story – highlighted the ongoing rally, confirming the peak at ₹71.38.

De‑rating factors

  • Oct 1 2025 – IPO listing at a 21 % discount – immediate drop on debut (shares settled 25 % lower).
  • Nov 17 2025 – Dec 15 2025 – 17 % fall (₹70.36 → ₹58.55) – no headline directly aligns; cause isn’t clear from the available news.

Pivots & turning points

  • IPO & listing discount (Sep‑Oct 2025) – set the initial valuation baseline.
  • Securing large‑scale infrastructure contracts (BHEL Feb 2026, Tata Projects Sep 2026) – marked a strategic shift toward high‑margin, big‑ticket projects.
  • May 27 2026 – appointment of Sabita Devi Kishorepuria as Executive Director (confirmed Aug 24) – signalled governance strengthening.
  • Nov 3‑7 2026 – Q2 FY27 earnings call (46 % revenue rise, 48 % profit jump) – reinforced the bullish narrative.

What moves this stock

  • Big fabricated‑steel or infrastructure orders (e.g., BHEL, Tata Projects) trigger sharp upside.
  • IPO pricing dynamics – a steep discount at listing creates immediate downside but can also spark a rebound as investors view the dip as a buying opportunity.
  • Quarterly earnings that beat revenue or profit expectations (especially strong steel demand) provide a secondary lift.

544060.one: *Re‑rated from ~Rs 110 (Mar‑2026 low) to ~Rs 170 (Nov‑2026) as strong retail expansion and earnings beats outweighed a fraud scare and short‑term margin pressure.*
544060.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 12 Aug 2026 – Q1 FY27 results: Revenue surged ≈ 60 % (₹120 Cr) and PAT rose to ₹9 Cr; stock jumped +33 % in August (150.9 → 200.7).
  • 20 Mar 2026 – Investor presentation: Comprehensive deck highlighted store rollout and inventory hedge; price rallied +32 % from early‑Mar to mid‑Apr (113.9 → 150.3).
  • 24 Sep 2026 – Flagship 10,000 sq ft store in Surat: New flagship opened; stock hit upper‑circuit on 28‑29 Sep and rose +15 % through Oct (173 → 199.4).
  • 11 Oct 2026 – Q2 2026 earnings: Revenue up 20 % YoY to ₹636.48 Cr, EPS ₹13.7; reinforced the upward trend set by the September store news.

De‑rating factors

  • 05 Mar 2025 – Employee fraud disclosed (₹2 Cr): Shares fell ≈ 6 % on the day and the broader 4‑week slide was ‑26 % (Feb 10 → Mar 10, 187.2 → 138.1).

Pivots & turning points

  • Capital‑allocation focus (08 Jan 2026) – analyst note praised disciplined investment, setting tone for later expansion.
  • Q4 FY26 profit jump (14 May 2026, +36 %) – signaled improving margins before the 2026‑02 dip.
  • Store‑expansion plan (05 Nov 2026) – three new Gujarat stores announced for FY27, underpinning the Q2 FY27 revenue surge.
  • Surge in daily sales at Surat store (07 Nov 2026, ₹50 L daily) – concrete proof of retail traction.

What moves this stock

  • Earnings beats & high‑growth revenue reports (Q1 FY27, Q2 2026) trigger strong upside.
  • Major store openings or flagship launches (Surat flagship) generate short‑term spikes and upper‑circuit activity.
  • Governance shocks (fraud disclosures) produce sharp downside, even when fundamentals remain solid.

544599.html:
One‑line story: De‑rated from Rs 560.3 to Rs 398.25 as post‑IPO weakness, raw‑material cost pressure and mixed earnings outweighed product‑launch and capacity‑expansion tailwinds.

Re‑rating factors (price rises)

Date (approx.) News Price reaction
May 11 – Jun 8 2026 (4‑week +14 %) Launch of the Superman Legacy Shield helmet (Jun 8) and a sector‑wide rally for auto ancillary stocks plus a BJP‑led West Bengal policy win (Jun 9) Stock jumped from ~₹438 to ~₹501.

544997.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 326 (Nov 2024) to Rs 771 (Nov 2026) as a series of profit‑driven earnings beats and a strategic robotics investment sparked strong upside, while the early‑2026 pull‑back remains unexplained by headlines.*
544997.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 12 May 2026 – Alphadroid investment: Shree Vasu Logistics announced a joint investment with Alkemi Growth Capital to scale robotics in healthcare and supply‑chain logistics.
    Price reaction: Share price jumped from ≈ ₹ 537 (11 May) to ≈ ₹ 695 (8 Jun) – a +30 % 4‑week gain (largest move with a matching news event).

  • 4 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 results: Profit surged +388 % YoY to ₹5.08 cr on 43 % revenue growth, 3PL profit hit ₹13.68 cr, and assets rose to ₹302.81 cr.
    Price reaction: Shares climbed from ≈ ₹ 750 (early Nov) to ₹ 771 by 6 Nov 2026, reinforcing the upward trend.

  • 5 Nov 2026 – Investor call highlights: Management emphasized “strong growth in revenue, EBITDA and PAT driven by new client additions and repeat business in new territories.”
    Price reaction: The rally continued, pushing the stock toward its 2‑year high of ₹ 881 (Oct 2026) before settling at ₹ 771.

De‑rating factors

  • 19 Jan 2026 – Unexplained sell‑off: Shares fell from ₹ 673 (19 Jan) to ₹ 531 (16 Feb) (‑21 %). No headline in the provided list directly explains this dip.

Pivots & turning points

  • Strategic robotics partnership (May 2026): Entry into automation signaled a new growth avenue beyond traditional 3PL services.
  • Q2 FY27 earnings beat (Nov 2026): Massive profit acceleration and cash‑flow improvement shifted market sentiment from “sell” (30 Oct) to “buy‑back” optimism.
  • Share‑holding pattern disclosure (31 Aug 2026): Transparency on promoter/FII/DII stakes helped stabilize the stock after earlier volatility.

What moves this stock

  • Earnings surprises: Quarterly profit jumps (especially >300 % YoY) trigger immediate price appreciation.
  • Strategic tech/automation deals: Investments that promise cost efficiencies (e.g., the Alphadroid robotics tie‑up) generate volume‑backed rallies.
  • Analyst rating shifts: Downgrades (30 Oct 2026) followed by strong results quickly reverse sentiment, underscoring the market’s sensitivity to valuation commentary.

544459.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 229 to Rs 272 as early post‑IPO volatility gave way to a sharp rally driven by capacity expansion, profit surges and blockbuster sales numbers, though the stock remains highly news‑sensitive.*
544459.html:

  • 2025‑08‑01 – Shares debut at a 14‑15 % premium to the IPO price (≈ Rs 215) → +5 % on debut.
  • 2025‑08‑20 / 21 – Q1 profit jumps 174 % to ₹25 cr, revenue +22 % → +9‑11 % rally.
  • 2026‑04‑28 – Q4 FY26 results released (revenue and PAT beat) → +26 % over the next four weeks (Rs 163.58 → Rs 205.75).
  • 2026‑06‑08 – New Mumbai plant adds 4,000 kg capacity → +28 % from Jul 20 to Aug 17 (Rs 211.29 → Rs 269.58).
  • 2026‑09‑23 – Technical strength lifts stock to 52‑week high; investment in Ratnaveer announced Sep 28 → +68 % to the 2‑yr high of Rs 423.3 on Oct 12.
  • 2026‑10‑02 – Brokerage upgrades to Buy → supports continuation of the Oct rally.

De‑rating factors

  • 2025‑11‑10 → 2025‑12‑08 – No major positive news; price fell ‑15 % (Rs 227.62 → Rs 193.92).
  • 2026‑02‑09 → 2026‑03‑09 – Despite a profit jump on Feb 10, the share slipped ‑14 % (Rs 217.84 → Rs 187.61); the cause isn’t clear from headlines.

Pivots & turning points

  • IPO (Jul 2025) – Capital raise of Rs 360 cr set the market base.
  • Management continuity – Re‑appointment of MD Pankajkumar Jagawat on Mar 19 2026 reinforced strategic stability.
  • Capacity boost – June 2026 Mumbai plant expansion (4,000 kg) signalled scaling of production.

  • Guidance reaffirmation – FY27 revenue target of ₹3,200‑3,500 cr confirmed on Nov 7 2026, anchoring investor expectations.

What moves this stock

  • Capacity and production upgrades – New manufacturing capacity triggers strong upside.
  • Quarterly earnings surprises – Double‑digit profit or revenue jumps translate into immediate price spikes.
  • Analyst upgrades / sector rallies – Buy ratings and broader jewellery‑stock rallies (e.g., PC Jeweller rally Oct 16 2026) provide a catalyst for large gains.

538836.one: *De‑rated from Rs 913 → Rs 498 as earnings collapsed, raw‑material cost pressure mounted and dividend news sparked only fleeting rallies.*
538836.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 02 Sep 2025 – ₹20 dividend announced – price jumped from ~₹572 to ~₹666 (+16 %) by 22 Sep 2025.
  • 24 Dec 2025 – ₹147 cr solar‑PV plant order from MPUVNL – shares rose ~2 % the next trading day.
  • 20 May 2026 – Q4 2026 earnings call highlighted “strong revenue growth” – modest uptick in the week after the call (price moved higher but not a headline 4‑week swing).

De‑rating factors

  • 26 May 2025 – Q4 FY25 results: net loss ₹10.34 cr, revenue down – price slipped in the following weeks, setting the stage for the 18 % drop from 22 Dec 2025 to 19 Jan 2026.
  • 05 Aug 2026 – Q1 FY27 net loss widens to ₹23.4 cr – share price fell sharply in August‑September 2026.
  • 23 Oct 2026 – Q2 FY27 conference call & “Sell” rating – stock slid to a 2‑year low of ₹488.5, testing the lower band of its range.
  • 04 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 results: profit down 93 %, revenue up only 5.5 % – further pressure on the price in November 2026.

Pivots & turning points

  • Dividend policy shift (₹20 per share, Sep 2025).
  • Entry into solar‑PV business (₹147 cr order, Dec 2025).
  • CMD re‑appointment – Jawahar Lal Oswal (08 Aug 2026).
  • Targeting ₹17‑18 cr solar revenue in FY28 (Nov 2026).
  • Management’s warning on raw‑material cost inflation & macro headwinds (Q2 FY27 call, Nov 2026).

What moves this stock

  • Dividend announcements – investors reward higher payouts with short‑term rallies.
  • Large contract wins (especially non‑apparel, e.g., solar projects) – give modest, positive price bumps.
  • Earnings disappointments and downgrades – profit collapses, widening losses, and “Sell” ratings trigger sharp sell‑offs.

Overall, Monte Carlo’s price swings over the past two years have been driven more by earnings volatility and rating changes than by its core apparel operations.

543425.one: *De‑rated from Rs 2100 to Rs 839 as a series of contract wins, an acquisition and mixed earnings cues failed to sustain earlier rally‑fuelled optimism.*
543425.html:

De‑rating factors

  • 2024‑11‑04 → 2024‑12‑02 – 4‑week drop of ‑20 % (2 058 → 1 644). No headline in the supplied list covers this period, so the cause isn’t clear from the headlines.
  • 2025‑12‑29 → 2026‑01‑26 – ‑25 % (1 701 → 1 276) as the stock fell after the 2026‑01‑15 acquisition of a stake in Iwayplus Private Ltd; the market appeared to discount the deal’s integration risk.
  • 2026‑02‑09 → 2026‑03‑09 – ‑24 % (1 234 → 934) with no contemporaneous news, so the driver is unclear.

  • 2026‑04‑15 – Q4 2026 results released (providing fresh earnings visibility).

  • 2026‑11‑04 – Q1 FY27 revenue up 14.9% to ₹139.7 cr; earnings call highlighted strong YoY growth and a robust order book, reinforcing a short‑term upside.

What moves this stock

  • Contract wins / MoUs with large infrastructure players (e.g., Mumbai Metro) trigger sharp upside as the market prices in recurring software‑as‑a‑service revenue.
  • Strategic acquisitions (Iwayplus) can cause volatility; investors react to perceived integration risk more than immediate earnings impact.
  • Analyst upgrades / price‑target revisions (June‑July 2026) produce quick, sizable rallies, especially when paired with positive earnings commentary.

544540.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 193.75 to Rs 192.57 as IPO enthusiasm, multi‑crore orders and new plants lifted the stock, while margin pressure, cash‑flow strain and a board‑secretary resignation pulled it back.*
544540.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Oct 2025 – IPO launch & anchor book – Sep 24‑Oct 1 IPO pricing (Rs 194‑204) and Rs 151 cr anchor funding; share price jumped from Rs 193.75 (Oct 6) to a 2‑yr high of Rs 327.95 (Nov 3) (+69%).

De‑rating factors

  • Dec 2025 – Jan 2026 – Guidance & valuation concerns – maintaining FY26 revenue guidance (Jan 21) and a “34 % cheaper” note (Jan 23) preceded a slide from Rs 294.8 (Dec 22) to Rs 184.1 (Jan 19) (‑38%).
  • Feb – Mar 2026 – Market uncertainty – price‑movement clarification (Apr 9) and lack of fresh catalysts saw the stock fall from Rs 209.95 (Feb 2) to Rs 161.34 (Mar 2) (‑23%).
  • Oct – Nov 2026 – Cash‑flow & governance stress – CS resignation (Oct 14), negative cash‑flow alerts (Nov 4‑5) and margin dip (Nov 5) preceded the drop from Rs 253.62 (Oct 5) to Rs 192.57 (Nov 2) (‑24%).

Pivots & turning points

  • IPO (Sep 2025) – capital raise and public‑market debut.
  • Large contract wins – Rs 130 cr (Oct 2025) and Rs 165 cr (Jun 2026).
  • New manufacturing capacity – Tirupati plant (May 2026) and Ghiloth line (Oct 2026).
  • Financial strain – margins squeezed by steel costs, cash‑flow turned negative (Nov 2026).
  • Governance event – Company Secretary’s resignation (Oct 2026).

What moves this stock

  • IPO‑related news and anchor‑book funding – triggers sharp upside.
  • Multi‑crore order announcements & capacity expansions – sustain rallies.
  • Margin pressure, cash‑flow deterioration and governance shocks – generate pronounced sell‑offs.

503722.one: *De‑rated from Rs 162.78 to Rs 98.67 as earnings momentum stalled and a series of operational setbacks eroded sentiment.*
503722.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • 19 May 2026 – FY26 PAT up 33%: “Banswara Syntex FY26 PAT rises 33% to ₹28.40 cr.” The stock rallied from the low‑120s to a 4‑week high of ₹123.64 (May 2026).

  • 21 Sep 2026 – 19 Oct 2026: “Promoter group member sells 6,861 shares” (3 Sep) followed by a plant fire (27 Oct) and the resignation of Garment Head Rahul Bhaduria (30 Oct). Share price slid from ₹108.73 to ₹94.61 (‑13%).

What moves this stock

  • Earnings surprises / PAT growth: Strong profit updates (Feb 2026, May 2026) trigger sharp upside.
  • Strategic shifts (exports, fabric‑garment mix): Positive guidance on new markets lifts the share.
  • Operational or governance setbacks (share sales, plant fire, director resignations): Negative news quickly erodes the rally and drives downside.

544633.one: *Round‑trip: from the Rs 52 IPO price (Dec 2025) up to a 2‑yr high of Rs 108 in May 2026, then back to Rs 68 in Nov 2026 as capacity‑expansion news lifted the stock while cash‑flow and circuit‑breaker volatility dragged it down.*
544633.html:
Re‑rating factors

  • Feb 5‑9 2026 – ALCU Industries goes commercial & announces 18,000 t capacity boost – stock jumped from Rs 44.5 (26 Jan) to Rs 53.4 (23 Feb) (+20%).
  • Apr 7‑8 2026 – Q4 FY26 results: sales ₹597.9 cr (+57.5% YoY), PAT ₹19.6 cr (+55%) – shares surged from Rs 52.3 (30 Mar) to Rs 87.3 (27 Apr) (+67%).
  • May 12‑13 2026 – Q4 FY26 profit and revenue beat – price rose from Rs 88.8 (18 May) to Rs 107.3 (15 Jun) (+21%).

De‑rating factors

  • Oct 5‑30 2026 – Series of circuit‑breaker alerts and a Rs 35 cr operating cash outflow disclosed in Q2 FY27 – share fell from Rs 98.1 (5 Oct) to Rs 67.8 (2 Nov) (‑31%).
  • Nov 6 2026 – Lower‑circuit breach (‑9.15% in one session) – further confirmed the down‑trend after the cash‑flow news.

Pivots & turning points

  • Jan 13 2026 – Revised manufacturing schedule for subsidiary ALCU (pre‑commercial ramp‑up).
  • Feb 5‑7 2026 – ALCU starts commercial production in Gujarat – marked the first major capacity‑realisation.
  • Apr 7 2026 – Strong Q4 FY26 earnings – shifted market focus to execution rather than just fundraising.
  • Nov 4‑7 2026 – Q2 FY27 results (52.5% revenue growth, 42% PAT rise) and announcement of CTC output by Dec 2026 – attempted to reset the narrative after the October slump.

What moves this stock

  • Capacity‑expansion milestones (e.g., ALCU commercial launch, 18 kt capacity plan) – the market rewards tangible production upside.
  • Quarterly earnings that beat revenue/PAT expectations – sharp upside on strong top‑line growth.
  • Cash‑flow surprises and circuit‑breaker activity – negative cash‑flow or trading‑halt news triggers steep sell‑offs.

500171.html:

Re‑rating factors

  • 12‑14 Dec 2024 – Environmental nod & ₹6,500 cr soda‑ash greenfield approval – stock jumped from ~₹89 to ₹105 (+18 %) within four weeks.
  • 23 Mar – 20 Apr 2026 – FY26 revenue beat (1 Feb) & dividend anticipation – price climbed from the 4‑week low of ₹68.71 to ₹85.48 (+24 %).
  • 22 Jun – 20 Jul 2026 – Dividend announcement (14 Jun) & record‑date (17 Jun) – shares surged from ₹92.59 to ₹115.82 (+25 %).

De‑rating factors

  • 27 Jan – 24 Feb 2025 – 4‑week fall of 22 % (₹94.99 → ₹74.59). No adverse headline lines up; the dip likely reflects market worries about global oversupply noted in later earnings calls.
  • 14 Jul – 11 Aug 2025 – 4‑week fall of 17 % (₹93.40 → ₹77.26). Despite capacity‑addition news, the move is unexplained by the listed headlines.

Pivots & turning points

  • Dec 2024: Environmental clearance for the Gujarat soda‑ash plant (capacity to double).
  • Jul 2025: Lease renewal for Khadsaliya lignite mine and start of next‑phase capacity addition.
  • Jun 2026: Announcement of a ₹12 per‑share dividend and statutory‑auditor change.
  • Oct 2026: Commercial launch of bromine (2,800 t/yr) and diversification into specialty chemicals.
  • Nov 2026: 5‑star rating for Khadsaliya lignite mine; Q2 FY27 profit up 19 % (₹127 cr).

What moves this stock

  • Regulatory clearances for soda‑ash projects – market rewards the green‑field approvals with sharp rallies.
  • Dividend declarations – a ₹12/share payout triggered a 25 % jump in June‑July 2026.
  • Earnings beats / capacity expansions – revenue beats and new capacity (soda ash, bromine, lignite) lift sentiment, while oversupply concerns can quickly reverse gains.

512437.html:

Re‑rating factors

  • 17 Aug 2026 – Q1 results: Net profit jumped 377 % YoY; the stock surged from ~Rs 350 to Rs 562 within four weeks (+60 %).
  • 12 Oct 2026 – Upper‑circuit alert: Price climbed from Rs 454 to Rs 554 by early Nov (+22 %).
  • 5‑6 Nov 2026 – Q2 FY27 results: PAT up 270 % YoY, Apollo Cash monthly disbursements hit Rs 21 cr, loans rose 44 %, engineering team tripled; the stock stayed near Rs 550‑560 and earned a Strong‑Buy upgrade.

De‑rating factors

  • 3 Feb 2025 → 3 Mar 2025: Price fell from Rs 670 to Rs 515 (‑23 %). No headline explains this move.
  • 2 Mar 2026 → 30 Mar 2026: Price slipped from Rs 400 to Rs 339 (‑15 %). No matching news.
  • 4 May 2026 → 1 Jun 2026: Price dropped from Rs 370 to Rs 323 (‑13 %). No headline.
  • Nov 2024 → Feb 2025: From the 2024‑Nov peak Rs 797 down to Rs 670; cause not evident in the provided headlines.

Pivots & turning points

  • Q1 2026 profit surge (377 % YoY) signalled a successful rollout of Apollo Cash lending.
  • Q2 FY27 (Nov 2026) ramp‑up in disbursement volumes, revenue and profit, reinforcing the cash‑lending model.
  • 17 Sep 2026 – MD reappointment (Mikhil Innani) provided leadership continuity.
  • 15 Aug 2026 – Secretarial auditor resignation and 24 Sep 2026 – ₹2.94 cr cyber‑fraud flagged governance and risk concerns, but they did not halt the later price rally.

What moves this stock

  • Earnings beats & profit acceleration (Q1 2026, Q2 FY27) trigger strong upside.
  • Apollo Cash disbursement announcements (monthly Rs 21 cr, cumulative Rs 65 cr) are rewarded with price jumps.
  • Absence of material news or negative governance events tends to coincide with unexplained declines.

500335.html:
One‑line story: De‑rated from Rs 567 to Rs 337 as earnings slumped and trade‑price pressure outweighed occasional group‑wide upbeat news.

Re‑rating factors (price rises)

  • 2025‑04‑14 → 2025‑05‑12 (+16 %) – price climbed but no headline lines up; the cause isn’t clear from the listed news.
  • 2025‑11‑24 → 2025‑12‑22 (+18 %) – around the same time “ABG Birla Pivot: Rewiring Construction Commerce” (12 Oct 2025) signalled a strategic focus on construction‑related businesses, lifting sentiment for the cement arm.
  • 2026‑09‑28 → 2026‑10‑26 (+20 %) – coincides with Aditya Birla Capital’s Q2 profit up 38 % (30 Oct 2026) and the $1.5 bn rupee loan to buy Shell’s Solenergi unit (9 Oct 2026), both reinforcing the group’s cash‑rich image and nudging the cement stock higher.

De‑rating factors (price falls)

  • 2025‑02‑10 → 2025‑03‑10 (‑21 %) – no headline matches; the driver isn’t evident from the supplied list.
  • 2026‑02‑02 → 2026‑03‑02 (‑15 %) – despite MSCI inclusion (10 Feb 2026) and a capital raise in the housing finance arm, the fall has no clear news trigger.
  • 2026‑04‑13 → 2026‑05‑11 (‑20 %) – falls around UltraTech Cement’s 200 MTPA milestone speech (16 Apr 2026), suggesting capacity expansion that may have raised concerns about oversupply and margin pressure for Birla Corporation.

  • UltraTech Cement 200 MTPA milestone (16 Apr 2026) – signals large capacity additions in the group’s core cement business.
  • ABG Birla Pivot: Rewiring Construction Commerce (9 Dec 2025) – a strategic shift toward construction‑related services.
  • MSCI global‑index addition (10 Feb 2026) – broad‑based visibility boost for the group.
  • Birla Corporation Q2 FY27 profit fall 58.6 % (1 Nov 2026) – a stark earnings warning that reinforced the downtrend.

What moves this stock

  • Group‑wide construction or cement capacity announcements (e.g., UltraTech milestones, construction‑commerce pivots).
  • Quarterly earnings surprises – especially sharp profit declines (Nov 2026) or strong group earnings (Oct 2026).
  • Macro‑level sentiment shifts reflected in index inclusions or large‑scale financing news (MSCI addition, housing‑finance capital raise).

Overall, Birla Corporation’s price has been more sensitive to macro‑level group developments and earnings outcomes than to isolated news items.

543384.one: *Re‑rated from Rs 158.8 to Rs 353 as a series of earnings beat‑outs, UK expansion and a fashion‑segment surge repeatedly lifted the stock.*

What moves this stock

543212.html:
